item.title: Two men, two women wounded in Brooklyn bar lounge shooting
item.description: Gunfire erupted inside Richard's Restaurant and Bar on Avenue L near E. 94th St. in Canarsie about 5 a.m. Sunday, police said.

item.description: "It is, in fact, an improvised explosive device that could have caused serious injury or death," NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said on social media.

item.title: Panhandler killed in Brooklyn hit-and-run was struck by two SUV drivers: NYPD
item.description: A second light-colored SUV, also going west on Linden, struck the victim as he lay in the roadway, cops said. Neither driver remained at the scene.

item.title: ‘Country Joe’ McDonald, Woodstock counterculture hero, dies at age 84
item.description: “Country Joe” McDonald, whose off-the-cuff rendition of “I Feel Like I’m Fixin’ To Die Rag” at the 1969 Woodstock Festival became a Viet Nam antiwar anthem, has died.

item.title: Mike Brown blasts Knicks ‘self-inflicted’ wounds in 110-97 loss to Lakers
item.description: In the wire-to-wire victory, the Lakers led by as many as 23 point, capitalizing on turnovers, offensive rebounds and inexplicable fouls to hand a rolling Knicks team just its sixth loss since Jan. 20.

item.title: Readers sound off on foreign policy failures, a Texas primary and the World Series
item.description: Bloomington, Ind.: The primary goal of the April 1961 Bay of Pigs invasion was the removal of Fidel Castro’s Communist government in Cuba. Planned by the CIA and approved by President John F. Kennedy, the operation relied on a force of U.S.-trained Cuban exiles who would land on the island and ignite a popular uprising. The expectation in Washington was that ordinary Cubans, once given a spark, would rise up and overthrow Castro, weakening Soviet influence in the Western Hemisphere.
